classification.difficultyReason: Construct successive reflections, retain vertices lying on the second axis, then compare final displacements across both diagrams to connect their identical translations with equal axis separation.

content.prompt: Answer these questions on square grid paper.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Reflect triangle $ABC$ in line $\ell_1$ and then reflect the image in $\ell_2$. Label the first image $A'C'B'$ and the second $A''B''C''$.

spec.description: Twelve-column, five-row square grid with triangle ABC and two labelled vertical reflection axes. A blank-grid template cannot express the supplied triangle and axes. Ordinary source blue marks are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Relative to the unprinted lower-left grid corner, A=(3,4), B=(3,1), C=(1,1); reflection axes are x=6 and x=8. No coordinates or coordinate axes are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original triangle and reflection axes are visible.

answer.short: The first and second images are shown in the diagram.
answer.worked:
Reflect each vertex to the opposite side of $\ell_1$, keeping its perpendicular distance from the line unchanged, then join the image vertices. $A'$ and $B'$ are 3 squares right of $\ell_1$; $C'$ is 5 squares right of it.

Reflect these vertices in $\ell_2$. $A''$ and $B''$ are 1 square left of $\ell_2$; $C''$ is 3 squares left of it. Keep each vertex at its original height and join the vertices.

spec.description: Complete self-contained reflection construction. First image uses red dashed edges and second image green solid edges to distinguish the stages.
spec.mathematics: First image A'=(9,4), B'=(9,1), C'=(11,1). Second image A''=(7,4), B''=(7,1), C''=(5,1), all relative to the unprinted lower-left grid corner.

children.label: b
children.prompt: This time, reflect triangle $ABC$ in line $\ell_3$ and then reflect the image in $\ell_4$. Label the first image $A'C'B'$ and the second $A''B''C''$ as before.

spec.description: Twelve-column, five-row square grid with the same triangle and a different pair of labelled vertical reflection axes. A blank-grid template cannot express the supplied triangle and axes. Ordinary source blue marks are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Relative to the unprinted lower-left grid corner, A=(3,4), B=(3,1), C=(1,1); reflection axes are x=5 and x=7. No coordinate axes or numerical coordinates are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original triangle and reflection axes are visible.

answer.short: The first and second images are shown in the diagram. $A'=A''$ and $B'=B''$ lie on $\ell_4$.
answer.worked:
Reflect each vertex in $\ell_3$, keeping its perpendicular distance from the line unchanged. $A'$ and $B'$ are 2 squares right of $\ell_3$, on $\ell_4$; $C'$ is 4 squares right of $\ell_3$.

Reflect this image in $\ell_4$. Points on the axis stay fixed, so $A''=A'$ and $B''=B'$. Place $C''$ 2 squares left of $\ell_4$, at the same height as $C'$, then join the vertices.

spec.description: Complete reflection construction with both labels retained at each fixed shared vertex on the second axis. First image dashed red, second image solid green.
spec.mathematics: First image A'=(7,4), B'=(7,1), C'=(9,1). Second image A''=(7,4), B''=(7,1), C''=(5,1). The first two image vertices lie on the second reflection axis.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Describe the translation that takes triangle $ABC$ to triangle $A''B''C''$ in both parts a and b. What do you notice?

answer.short:
Both are 4 units right.

The pairs of reflection lines are both 2 units apart, so they produce the same translation.
answer.worked:
Compare corresponding original and final vertices in each diagram: every final vertex is 4 squares to the right at the same height. Both results are therefore translations 4 units right.

In each pair, the second axis is 2 units right of the first. Two successive reflections in these parallel lines produce a translation twice that distance, perpendicular to the lines.
